transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Vela CISO), Liam Harper (Vela Head of Platform), Sofia Nguyen (Vela DevOps), Markus Feld (Vela Legal)

Summary: quick intake to validate security gating for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Main asks: SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO/SAML flows and IdP, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, KMS integration (bring-your-own-key), and data residency / retention specifics. Team also wants a perf sandbox for throughput and latencies.

Topics: SOC2 evidence; ISO27001; SAML/SSO; RBAC granularity and Admin roles; audit logs & log retention; KMS/BYOK; VPC/Private deployment options; SLA/backfills; pricing exposure for Dedicated.

Action items (auto): see action_items field below.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thank you for taking the time. Quick roll call, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Ravi our SE.
[00:08] Dana Ortiz: Hi, Dana here, CISO at Vela. We'll be a little tight on time, want to focus on gating questions.
[00:14] Liam Harper: Liam, platform. I'm the one who will actually touch the infra.
[00:18] Sofia Nguyen: Sofia, DevOps. Hoping to understand the KMS / VPC options.
[00:23] Markus Feld: Markus from legal, will listen for retention / eDiscovery needs.
[00:26] Ravi Patel: Great — thanks. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC model, audit logs + retention, encryption/KMS options and finally hosting variants (hosted/dedicated/private).
[00:35] Dana Ortiz: Perfect. Our quick elevator: Vela processes financial telemetry for SMB lenders, PII-ish, needs SOC2 Type II and ISO signals, and strict retention with 7 year hold for certain records. We're evaluating hosted first but likely will want Dedicated or Private for residency.
[00:51] Maya Chen: Understood. On SOC2 and ISO, we are SOC2 Type II, and we've got an ISO27001 cert—I'll share the latest reports. Note: there are redacted versions for public sharing, and we can coordinate an NDA for full artifacts.
[01:04] Dana Ortiz: Good — what specifically will you send? Full report or just system descriptions?
[01:09] Maya Chen: We'll send the SOC2 Type II report (redacted), plus the ISO27001 certification summary, and our security whitepaper that explains controls, key rotation, KMS integrations. I'll put links in the follow-up.
[01:19] Liam Harper: On SSO — we run Okta, looking for SAML or OIDC with just-in-time provisioning. Also we need SCIM support for user provisioning.
[01:29] Ravi Patel: We support both SAML and OIDC. SCIM is supported for provisioning and user-sync, mapping to RBAC roles. Quick note: our SAML assertion mapping can sync groups to roles, so you can map Okta groups to admin/ops/readonly within Redwood Console.
[01:44] Sofia Nguyen: Is there support for IdP-initiated flows? Also, multi-tenant role separation — can we lock per-environment access?
[01:52] Ravi Patel: Yes IdP and SP initiated. For isolation, you can pin projects to dedicated instances; RBAC is per-organization and per-route, so you can scope teams to infra — not a free-form nested policy engine but we do have granular role mappings and API keys scoped to models/routes.
[02:09] Dana Ortiz: Audit logs — we need immutable logs, tamper evidence, and at least 3 year retention with export capability. Do you maintain append-only logs or integrate with our SIEM?
[02:21] Maya Chen: We produce comprehensive audit logs covering API calls, console actions, auth events, KMS key usage. Logs are shipped to our internal storage, but we also provide integrations to forward logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/ELK). For Dedicated and Private deployments you can route logs to your collector directly.
[02:40] Liam Harper: When you say KMS key usage — how does BYOK work? Are we provisioning keys in our cloud KMS and Redwood never sees plaintext?
[02:49] Ravi Patel: For BYOK we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs in Private envs. The runtime performs envelope encryption; the customer KMS performs key wrapping/unwrapping. Redwood does not persist plaintext keys — we hold only wrapped keys and ephemeral decrypt tokens. For hosted customers we manage the envelope flow but with Dedicated/Private you can bring your own key material and control rotation.
[03:12] Sofia Nguyen: Any latency or throughput impact for BYOK on token generation? We need <60ms median token latency at p95 ideally.
[03:20] Ravi Patel: There's a small initial key unwrap on session start, but KMS calls are cached and we use a short-lived envelope token for subsequent inference. So per-token latency isn't impacted in steady state; the unwrap adds to cold-starts. We'll show instrumentation in the perf run.
[03:36] Dana Ortiz: Does Redwood hold customer data for training or model improvement?
[03:40] Maya Chen: No, we have an explicit policy: no customer data is used for model training unless contracted and opt-in. We'll include that language in the security docs.
[03:47] Markus Feld: From legal side — we need to see data residency options and contract language about data deletion/erasure and eDiscovery. Are there support tools for data deletion requests?
[03:57] Ravi Patel: Yes — we offer deletion APIs and retention configurations per project. For Hosted we have configurable retention windows; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention to zero or route all logs to your S3. eDiscovery can be supported via export workflows; we'll draft the exact pipeline in the follow-up.
[04:14] Liam Harper: On dedicated vs private — cost aside, what's the operational difference for our infra team? We want predictable throughput, and the ability to run custom quantization/profiles later.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Dedicated is our reserved pool model — you get dedicated GPU pools in Redwood-managed infra, single-tenant layer, with predictable throughput and SLA. Private gives you the control plane managed by Redwood but the data plane in your VPC or on-prem, with full BYOK and network isolation. Dedicated is faster to stand up; Private requires more network ops but gives maximum control.
[04:45] Dana Ortiz: Does Dedicated allow bringing keys into our KMS? I want to ensure we can rotate keys without Redwood having access.
[04:51] Ravi Patel: For Dedicated we support customer KMS — it's slightly different per cloud. You can grant Redwood role-based access to perform the envelope unwrap, or with Private you can keep KMS entirely in your account and we run the agent in your VPC so the plaintext never leaves. We'll include a matrix in the follow-up.
[05:07] Sofia Nguyen: Audit log retention — is there a hard cap on retention for hosted customers? We might need 7 years which is longer than typical.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Hosted has tiers; standard retention is 90/365 days depending on plan, with add-ons to extend or export to your storage for long-term retention. For multi-year retention we'd typically route logs to your S3 or GCS bucket via secure export and lifecycle rules.
[05:30] Dana Ortiz: Ok. On RBAC — need separation of duties: operators vs auditors vs security admins. Can you show or export role mappings?
[05:38] Ravi Patel: You can map IdP groups to our roles and we provide an audit of who has which role. We also log access grants and provide a roles CSV export. For stricter use cases we can recommend a custom role set for Private deployments.
[05:50] Liam Harper: SLA and incident handling — what is your post-incident log replay for Forensics? Will you expose telemetry to our SOC?
[05:59] Maya Chen: Our SLA includes incident notification, triage, and we provide post-incident reports. For forensic needs we can provide raw logs — again, Dedicated/Private gives more direct access. We also have signed processes for red-team findings and CVE disclosures.
[06:11] Dana Ortiz: Encryption in transit and at rest — are there any exceptions for model weights or KV cache?
[06:17] Ravi Patel: All in-transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we encrypt model artifacts and KV cache. Model weights on hosted are encrypted; in Dedicated we manage keys but can integrate with your KMS for BYOK. For Private, artifacts remain in your network. There are no cleartext persistence exceptions.
[06:32] Sofia Nguyen: Is there support for hardware HSMs for FIPS / FedRAMP style keys?
[06:36] Ravi Patel: We can integrate with HSM-backed KMS providers — in Private you'd run your HSM. For Hosted we can integrate with cloud HSM-backed KMS. We can share architecture notes.
[06:46] Markus Feld: Retention/Legal hold — we need to be sure legal can assert holds and that data isn't auto-purged while hold exists.
[06:54] Maya Chen: You can place legal holds at the project level which override lifecycle rules. We'll show the API in the sandbox.
[07:02] Liam Harper: Any preview of cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our expected footprint (approx 1M tokens/day, bursty)?
[07:10] Maya Chen: I'll send a usage estimate spreadsheet. Dedicated typically reduces unit cost at scale but has monthly commit requirements. Private has higher setup but predictable op costs.
[07:20] Dana Ortiz: Competitors — we did a bake-off and saw BigCloudAI had easier AD sync, NimbusServe had a full on-prem image. Why choose Redwood for security?
[07:30] Maya Chen: We lean on production-first controls — transparent SOC/ISO evidence, BYOK, granular RBAC, and a unified runtime across deployment types. Also our audit/export tooling is designed for long retention export.
[07:40] Sofia Nguyen: For the perf sandbox — can we get a Dedicated-style env with our KMS keys attached to emulate BYOK?
[07:46] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can provision a sandbox Dedicated pool and attach an ephemeral customer KMS flow. Some constraints apply but we'll document them.
[07:55] Dana Ortiz: One last question — do you ever train on customer prompts by default? We need clear committed policy.
[08:01] Maya Chen: No — we will not use customer data for training unless explicitly contracted and opt-in. We'll include a binding clause in the T&Cs draft.
[08:08] Markus Feld: We'll need to review the T&Cs and DPA. Can you send redlined examples?
[08:13] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include a DPA and example SLA.
[08:16] Liam Harper: Great. Anything else?
[08:18] Sofia Nguyen: How quickly can we get the sandbox?
[08:21] Ravi Patel: We can kick it off once we have NDA for the SOC docs and your KMS info — I can start provisioning in parallel. Plan for ~5 business days to get a dedicated sandbox up.
[08:31] Dana Ortiz: Good. Recap?
[08:34] Maya Chen: Recap — Maya to share SOC2/ISO and security whitepaper; Ravi to provision dedicated sandbox with BYOK flow and perf harness; Dana to share retention/legal hold specs; Markus to review DPA and highlight contract points. We'll target follow-ups and dates in the next steps.
[08:50] Markus Feld: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:52] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with an email and tracker.

Notes / Links referenced: security-whitepaper.pdf (will share link), SOC2-typeII-redacted.pdf (NDA for full), dedicated-sandbox-invite (to be sent), perf-harness-spec.xlsx (internal).

End of transcript.
